name: Contra (魂斗罗)
blurb: Konami's 1987 run-and-gun shooter, famous for the 30-lives Konami Code
title: Contra: The 30 Lives Code, Versions and History
description: Contra is Konami's 1987 arcade run-and-gun shooter, ported to the Famicom/NES in 1988, where up-up-down-down-left-right-left-right-B-A gave 30 lives.
answer: Contra is a side-scrolling run-and-gun shooter released by Konami in arcades in 1987 and on the Famicom and NES in February 1988, in which one or two commandos fight their way through an alien army. On the NES, entering the Konami Code (up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, B, A) at the title screen raises your lives from 3 to 30. In China, where it is called 魂斗罗 (Hun Dou Luo), it was one of the most played games on Famicom clones and in 1990s arcades, and the original has been re-released many times, most recently in the 2019 Contra Anniversary Collection.

body: You control Bill Rizer and Lance Bean, two soldiers who run, jump and shoot through jungle, base and alien-hive stages to destroy the Red Falcon organization. The Japanese story sets it in the year 2633 on a fictional archipelago; the US manual moved it to the present-day Amazon. One hit kills you, so lives matter.

ul: S: spread gun, five shots fanning out, the favourite
F: fireball that travels in a corkscrew
R: faster bullets; B: a short barrier that makes you invincible

body: The Famicom/NES version has eight stages, the arcade seven. The Japanese Famicom cartridge used Konami's VRC2 chip and added cutscenes and animated backgrounds that the cheaper NES board lacked.

The Konami Code was created by Kazuhisa Hashimoto while porting Gradius to the NES, as a way to make testing easier. Contra made it famous: entering up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, B, A on the title screen, then Start, gives 30 lives. It is still called the "Contra Code" or "30 Lives Code". Chinese players often remember it as "上上下下左右左右BABA"; pressing B, A twice also works.

sections.h: Why it was huge in China
body: The arcade game reached China's coastal-city game halls in the late 1980s, but the Famicom version is what most people remember. Nearly every multi-game cartridge for Subor and other clones included it, and two-player co-op with a sibling or neighbour was a standard after-school scene. Unofficial Chinese hacks also circulated under other names; they are not part of Konami's series.

faq.q: How do you get 30 lives in Contra?
faq.a: On the title screen press up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, B, A, then Start.

faq.q: How many levels does Contra have?
faq.a: Eight on the Famicom and NES, seven in the arcade version.

faq.q: Why is Contra called Probotector in Europe?
faq.a: In PAL regions the NES version was released as Probotector, with the heroes and some enemies redrawn as robots; the arcade version was sold there as Gryzor.
